thread:
Maya Chen: Heads up — Nimbus Bank wants a short pilot. Key asks: streaming via our JS SDK with transparent reconnect/backpressure, ephemeral creds rotation, and tool/function calls that return typed JSON for downstream systems. Also needs a burst SLA and a cost estimate for a 3-month pilot.

Ajay S: Quick Q — are they expecting server-sent events or websocket? Backpressure strategy differs.

Maya Chen: Websocket preferred. They mentioned edge proxy that will multiply connections. We need per-connection limits and connector guidance.

Tom Baker: For websocket + backpressure we usually recommend our streaming client with `maxInflight` + token-based flow control. Example snippet: 

```js
const client = new RedwoodSDK({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, streaming: true });
await client.connect({ url: 'wss://inference.redwood.com/v1/stream' });
client.on('message', (msg) => {
  // apply backpressure: pause reading if queue length > N
});
```

Ajay S: For ephemeral creds we can do short-lived tokens via STS or our signed session tokens. Recommend 15m TTL for pilot. We also need to confirm rotation path with their infra (who holds KMS).

Ellie (Solutions): On the structured tool calling: they require tools to return a strict schema so their downstream order processor won't break. We should provide a sample tool response schema and a validation shim.

Maya Chen: They asked whether we support schema validation out of the box or if they have to implement it client-side.

Tom Baker: We surface a `validateToolOutput(schema, payload)` helper in SDK v0.9.8 that uses AJV under the hood. Sending example: 

```json
{
  "tool": "payment-formatter",
  "result": {
    "amount_cents": 12345,
    "currency": "USD",
    "recipient_id": "acct_789"
  }
}
```

Tom Baker: SDK call looks like: `client.callTool('payment-formatter', { input })` — it returns `{ payload, meta }` and we run `validateToolOutput(schema, payload)` before downstream handoff.

Maya Chen: Great. For security questionnaire they flagged keys in logs and audit retention. Ajay — can you confirm our default log scrubbing and retention for Dedicated pilot?

Ajay S: Defaults: logs scrub API keys, session IDs; retention = 30 days in Standard. For pilot we can offer 90 days on Dedicated with contract. Also we can enable customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.

Ellie (Solutions): Pricing blunt ask from procurement: estimate for 3-month pilot with Reserved capacity (2 GPUs baseline, burst to 4 GPUs) + streaming egress. Can someone draft numbers? We need token-rate assumptions.

Tom Baker: I'll draft a ballpark: baseline reserved = $9,000/mo per GPU (internal), pilot discount 25% -> effective $13,500/mo for 2 GPUs. Burst billable at on-demand rate. Streaming egress estimate depends on conversation volume — need tokens/sec.

Maya Chen: I'll get token estimates from Nimbus (they said ~75 rps, average 150 tokens per req).

infra-bot: Quote generated: https://console.redwood.com/quotes/Q-2024-4598 (internal link) :white_check_mark:

Ajay S: One enterprise blocker flagged: their security team requires a SOC2 attestation and a data processing addendum. We have both but need to attach to the SOW. I'll surface the docs.

Ellie (Solutions): Action items: 1) Tom to produce pilot cost calc and sample SOW language. 2) Ajay to attach SOC2 & KMS options. 3) Maya to collect token/traffic profile and proxy topology. 4) Provide SDK sample + validation snippet for their infra team.

Maya Chen: Thanks — aiming to respond to procurement by EOD tomorrow. @Ajay @Tom can you try to have drafts by 10:00 PST tomorrow? :pray:

Tom Baker: Yep, will do. :thumbsup:

Ajay S: I'll upload SOC2 and KMS notes to the quote and ping procurement.

Maya Chen: If any show-stoppers surface, flag here and we can escalate to AE.

Ellie (Solutions): Also adding a short runbook for reconnect/backpressure to the shared drive. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/solutions/nimbus-runbook

Maya Chen: Perfect — closing loop after drafts are in. Thanks all. :rocket:
